verdict.rationale: Browserbase's own webhooks fire an HTTP POST automatically when a subscribed event happens. Endpoints can be managed from Settings or the SDK, and the product also markets agents that alert you the moment something breaks. That is real event-triggered behavior, but the only documented action is a notification to your endpoint, with no in-product rule definition, conditions, or action chaining; scheduled runs are time-based, not event-based, and earn no credit here. Missing for 10: a documented rules engine for defining event conditions, configurable in-product actions beyond webhook delivery, an event catalog detailing which events can trigger actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Browserbase webhooks send an HTTP POST to an endpoint you own as soon as a subscribed event happens, so you don't have to poll the API for status changes.
You can manage endpoints from Settings as well as through the SDK. Both act on the same webhooks.
Run agents that click through your product continuously and alert you the moment something breaks.
